entry.title: Fix stale UI copy
entry.content:
Fix stale UI copy

- Settings said media would join backups "in a later phase"; it has since P3
- the AI panels asked for an Anthropic key although any OpenAI-compatible
  provider works
- the Inbox file importer listed only two of the four packet kinds

entry.title: Add a not-found route
entry.content:
Add a not-found route

An unknown URL (a stale bookmark, a typo) rendered an empty main area with
no hint and no way back. A catch-all route now says so and links home.

entry.title: Store GIFs as uploaded instead of flattening them to one frame
entry.content:
Store GIFs as uploaded instead of flattening them to one frame

Image ingest re-encodes everything but SVG to WebP; for an animated GIF
that keeps only the first frame. GIFs are now kept as-is, like SVG.

entry.title: Simplify prerequisite cycle cleanup in recomputeUnlocks
entry.content:
Simplify prerequisite cycle cleanup in recomputeUnlocks

The cycle pass rebuilt the whole gate view (and wouldCycle rebuilt its
lookup map) once per prerequisite edge, and its comment claimed both edges
of a loop are dropped when the code (and its test) cut exactly one. A single
reachability walk over the cleaned edges keeps the behaviour, and the
comment now says what happens.

entry.title: Tell the unit drafter about proposals still awaiting review
entry.content:
Tell the unit drafter about proposals still awaiting review

"Draft more" before reviewing the previous draft handed the model only the
accepted and rejected rows, so it happily re-drafted the very items sitting
in the queue. Pending proposals now ride along as a "do not duplicate these
either" list.

entry.title: Convert captured notes correctly into list and media fields
entry.content:
Convert captured notes correctly into list and media fields

The capture converter stored a list field's text as a plain string (the
editor then showed it empty) and demanded text for image/audio fields, which
cannot be typed. List fields are now parsed into arrays and media fields are
left empty to attach later, matching the add-item form.

entry.title: Scope add-item synonyms to one template each
entry.content:
Scope add-item synonyms to one template each

The add-item form applied its "extra accepted answers" to every template of
the type, so on a Meaning + Reading type a meaning synonym became an
accepted reading — exactly the wrong-facet leak the packet importer refuses
and the item editor avoids. Multi-template types now get one synonym box per
template; single-template types look as before.

entry.title: Keep download object URLs alive until the browser has started saving
entry.content:
Keep download object URLs alive until the browser has started saving

Both downloads clicked a detached anchor and revoked the object URL
synchronously afterwards — Firefox and Safari can abort the save before it
starts in that case. One shared helper attaches the anchor, clicks it, and
revokes the URL a minute later.

entry.title: Show a boot-failure screen instead of a blank page
entry.content:
Show a boot-failure screen instead of a blank page

boot() had no error handling: if IndexedDB refused to open (another tab on a
newer schema, private browsing with storage blocked, disk full) the promise
rejected silently and the user saw an empty page with no explanation. The
failure is now rendered with the error text and a reload button.

entry.title: Ignore Enter while a native IME is composing
entry.content:
Ignore Enter while a native IME is composing

Anyone answering with a system Japanese/Chinese IME presses Enter to commit
the composition; the answer box treated that keystroke as submit and graded
a half-typed answer. The keydown handler now bails out while
nativeEvent.isComposing is set.

entry.title: Keep an item's lesson/active status in step with manual stage changes
entry.content:
Keep an item's lesson/active status in step with manual stage changes

Setting a stage on every card of a lesson-queue item scheduled the cards but
left the item in the lesson queue, so the next lesson batch offered an item
with nothing to teach. Manual updates now reconcile the item through the
same studyStatus rule the type designer and recomputeUnlocks use: nothing
left to teach means active, an untaught card means back to lessons.

entry.title: Stop the rich-text parser marking up plain text chunks
entry.content:
Stop the rich-text parser marking up plain text chunks

parseRichText classified every chunk from split(), matches and plain text
alike, by whether it started and ended with a marker. "* 3 *" rendered as
italic " 3 ", "== a ==" as a highlight, and a lone "`" or "**" vanished as
an empty mark. split() with one capture group alternates text and match, so
only the odd chunks are classified now.

entry.title: Validate hint fields and cloze answer fields in the type designer
entry.content:
Validate hint fields and cloze answer fields in the type designer

Two designs the designer accepted produced broken cards:
- a hint field that is the answer field: "show a hint" revealed the answer
- a typed or choice template whose answer field holds cloze sentences: the
  grader compares against sentence objects, so no answer is ever accepted
  (the packet importer already refused this; the designer did not)

entry.title: Free a deleted course's images and audio
entry.content:
Free a deleted course's images and audio

deleteCourse removed items, cards, logs, plans and proposals but never the
media its items pointed at, so every deleted picture course kept its blobs
in IndexedDB — and in every backup after — until someone pressed "Clean up
unused" in Settings. The ids are collected before the rows go and swept
after the transaction commits, through the same orphan check item deletion
uses.

entry.title: Remap suspended and burned cards when a ladder is edited
entry.content:
Remap suspended and burned cards when a ladder is edited

saveLadderEdit only touched cards in the review state. A suspended card
keeps its stage so it can resume, so after stages were removed its index
could sit past the new top — and resume() reads "past the top" as burned,
retiring the card instead of resuming it. Burned cards are now re-pointed at
the new top as well, so their stored index stays meaningful as the ladder
grows or shrinks.

entry.title: Drop stale session loads instead of letting them clobber a newer one
entry.content:
Drop stale session loads instead of letting them clobber a newer one

start() awaits the database several times; a load still in flight when the
user navigated to another course's reviews (or left the page) would finish
later and overwrite the newer session with the old course's cards. A load
generation counter, bumped by every start() and reset(), lets a stale load
bail out after each await. The lesson-batch and cram-pool loaders had the
same shape and get the same guard.

Regression test delays one course's due-card query and checks the newer
session survives.

entry.title: Fix comma-separated inputs eating the comma as you type
entry.content:
Fix comma-separated inputs eating the comma as you type

List fields, and the synonym / block-list boxes in the item editor, were
controlled inputs whose text was re-derived from the parsed array on every
keystroke: "cat," parsed to ['cat'] and rendered back as "cat", so a second
entry could only ever be pasted in. A new ListInput owns the raw text and
hands the parsed list up on each change, re-syncing only when the parent
supplies a different list.

entry.title: Course plans step 5: MCP tools and plan-aware snapshot
entry.content:
Course plans step 5: MCP tools and plan-aware snapshot

External assistants (Claude Desktop, Codex, any MCP client) can now do the
same job as the in-app planner. propose_course_plan writes a course-plan
packet — ordered units, 1-3 item types, optional proposed items per unit, and
the source material — and propose_items drops drafts into an existing course's
review queue, optionally targeting a unit. Both land in the Inbox and never
bypass the human gate; add_items/create_course keep their import-as-is
behaviour and now point at the review-queue tools for drafted content.

snapshot.json exposes each course's plan (units, what's open, dates, pending
proposals per unit), the current level, item levels, and a pending-proposals
count, so an assistant can see the syllabus structure before proposing.
list_courses prints the plan summary. 218 tests.

entry.title: Course plans step 4: plan page, review queue UI, entry points
entry.content:
Course plans step 4: plan page, review queue UI, entry points

Dashboard gains "From my material": paste a syllabus or notes, pick how units
release (by progress, by date, by hand), get an editable outline back — course
name, item types, units with item targets and dates — and create the course
with nothing in it yet. The new /plan/:courseId page is where the work
happens: one card per unit showing released/current/locked state, dates in
schedule mode, item and pass counts, a draft button with count and steer, and
the review queue with pending/rejected/accepted tabs. Rows show fields,
alternates, mnemonic, handle and prerequisites, a validation error or a
duplicate flag; accept, edit in a modal (fields, alternates, note, handle,
prerequisites), reject with an optional reason, restore, forget; accept-all and
reject-all per unit; release-mode switch and "Release next unit"; add a unit.

The Course page links to the plan and shows the current unit; the Dashboard
badges pending proposals; scheduled releases catch up at boot and whenever the
plan page opens. Verified in the browser against a pasted plan packet.
